segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר. תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִלְמָלֵי יָדֶיהָ מוּנָּחוֹת בְּעֵינֶיהָ כׇּל בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת — יָפֶה אַתָּה אוֹמֵר.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» With regard to any woman who did not perform the examination indicating her transition from ritual impurity to ritual purity on the seventh day from minḥa time onward, even if she performed an examination and found no blood that morning, the presumptive status of that woman is one of ritual impurity. It «is taught» in a baraita that the Rabbis «said to Rabbi Yehuda:» If the halakha «had» been that a woman who will immerse must keep her «hands placed in her eyes,» a euphemism for her vagina, for «the entire twilight» period, what «you say is fine.» It would be reasonable to assume that since she did not examine herself at the end of the day she has a presumptive status of ritual impurity.
